title: Correlation, Causation and Lines of Fit
seo_title: Algebra I Correlation and Lines of Fit Worksheets (TEKS A.4A)
standard_text: A.4A calculate, using technology, the correlation coefficient between two quantitative variables and interpret this quantity as a measure of the strength of the linear association; A.4B compare and contrast association and causation in real-world problems; A.4C write, with and without technology, linear functions that provide a reasonable fit to data to estimate solutions and make predictions for real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.4A–A.4C: scatter plots, the correlation coefficient, lines of fit, residuals and correlation versus causation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: r near ±1 is strong; near 0 is weak.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The correlation coefficient r is between −1 and 1. Close to 1 or −1: strong. Close to 0: weak.
  • The sign tells the direction: positive up, negative down.
  • A line of fit predicts y from x. Residual = actual − predicted.
  • Correlation is not causation: two things can rise together without one causing the other.

Examples

Example

r = −0.92

close to −1

Answer: strong negative

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking negative means weak−0.9 is strong.
Reading correlation as causationLook for another cause.
Residual the wrong wayActual minus predicted.

A line of best fit for age of a tree in years (x) and height in feet (y) is y = 1.2x + 3. What does the slope mean?
c: For each extra year, the height in feet increases by about 1.2 feet
For each extra year, the height in feet decreases by about 1.2 feet
For each extra year, the height in feet changes by about 3 feet
The height in feet is 1.2 when x = 0
items.e: The slope is the change in y for each 1 unit increase in x: for each extra year, the height in feet increases by about 1.2 feet.

A data point has a negative residual. Where is it compared with the line of best fit?
c: To the left of the line
items.e: Residual = actual − predicted. Negative means the actual value is smaller: below the line.

items.q: The line of best fit is ŷ = 1.5x + 14. A data point is (2, 20). What is its residual?
items.e: Predicted ŷ = 1.5 × 2 + 14 = 17. Residual = actual − predicted = 20 − 17 = 3.

items.q: A residual plot shows points scattered randomly above and below zero with no pattern. What does this suggest?
c: A linear model is a good fit
A linear model is a poor fit
items.e: Random residuals mean the line captures the pattern: a linear model fits well.

items.q: What is interpolation?
c: Predicting within the range of the data
Predicting beyond the range of the data
items.e: Interpolation predicts inside the data's range; extrapolation goes outside it.

items.q: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents have a strong positive correlation. Which conclusion is best?
c: Both probably rise in hot weather; ice cream does not cause drowning
The correlation must be a mistake
items.e: A third variable (hot weather) affects both. Correlation does not prove causation.

items.q: Two lines are fitted to the same data. Line A's residuals are mostly between −1 and 1; line B's are between −5 and 5. Which fits better?
items.e: Smaller residuals mean the predictions are closer to the data: line A.

items.q: The equation ŷ = 15x + 200 predicts monthly sales ŷ from advertising dollars x (in hundreds). If $400 is spent on ads, what are the predicted sales?
Which value of r is impossible?
items.e: r is always between −1 and 1, so 1.3 is impossible.

items.q: A scatter plot's points rise steeply and lie almost exactly on a line. Which value of r fits best?
items.e: Rising and very close to a line: r ≈ 0.98.

items.q: The correlation between two variables is −0.92. Which statement is true?
c: As one increases, the other tends to decrease, and the relationship is strong
The relationship is weak because r is negative
items.e: The sign shows direction (negative) and |−0.92| is close to 1: strong and negative.

items.q: Which is the best reason to look at a residual plot?
c: To find the mean of the data
To check whether a linear model is appropriate
items.e: Patterns in a residual plot show whether a line is the right model.

items.q: A data point is (5, 30) and the line predicts 34 at x = 5. What is the residual?
items.e: Residual = actual − predicted = 30 − 34 = −4.

items.q: A line of best fit has slope 0. What does that suggest?
items.e: A flat line predicts the same y for every x: x does not help predict y.
